title: ～が — marks the subject
summary: The particle that marks the subject of a sentence. It is used for new information and for events happening in front of you, and also marks the object of words like 好き and ほしい.

patterns.gloss: noun + が + predicate (雨が降っています)

patterns.form: 名詞＋が＋好き／ほしい／ある／できる
patterns.gloss: noun + が + 好き / ほしい / ある (犬が好きです)

body.p: As in 雨が降っています, it shows the subject of what is happening, or a person or thing newly brought into the conversation.
は marks the topic. が introduces or singles out the subject. For だれが来ましたか, the answer is 田中さんが来ました.

body.h: Marking the object of a feeling or ability
body.p: The object of words such as 好き, ほしい, 上手 and 分かる is marked by が (日本語が分かります).

examples.ja: 雨（あめ）が降（ふ）っています。
子（こ）どもが泣（な）いています。

pitfalls: Do not usually use を with 好き or ほしい (not 犬を好きです).
When the question word is the subject, use が, not は (だれが, 何が).
